# spinupwp_site_https (Resource)

HTTPS for a SpinupWP site. Destroying it disables HTTPS. SpinupWP doesn't return the certificate type, so after an import the first apply only records `type` and the certificate settings; it doesn't reissue the certificate.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let's Encrypt certificate. The domain must already point at the server.
resource "spinupwp_site_https" "example" {
  site_id = spinupwp_site.example.id
  type    = "webroot"
}

# Or a certificate validated through a DNS provider configured in SpinupWP,
# which works before the domain points at the server:
#
#   type            = "dns"
#   dns_provider_id = 12
#
# Or your own certificate. Bump private_key_wo_version to send a new key:
#
#   type                   = "custom"
#   certificate            = file("example.com.crt")
#   private_key_wo         = file("example.com.key")
#   private_key_wo_version = 1
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `site_id` (Number) ID of the site. Changing it moves the setting to another site.
- `type` (String) Certificate type: `webroot` (Let's Encrypt, needs the domain to point at the server), `dns` (Let's Encrypt validated through a DNS provider) or `custom`.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `certificate` (String) PEM certificate (with any intermediates). Required when `type` is `custom`.
- `dns_provider_id` (Number) ID of a team DNS provider. Required when `type` is `dns`.
- `private_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) PEM private key. Required when `type` is `custom`. Write-only: never stored in state.
- `private_key_wo_version` (Number) Version of `private_key_wo`. Change it to send a new value of the matching write-only argument; Terraform can't detect changes to write-only values on its own.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `certificate_expires` (String) When the certificate expires.
- `certificate_renews` (String) When SpinupWP renews the certificate.
- `id` (String) The site ID.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spinupwp_site_https.example
  id = "12345"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the SpinupWP site ID.
terraform import spinupwp_site_https.example 12345
```
